sources.title: Nigeria Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2, 30 June 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian needs and response for 1 January–30 June 2025; report published 30 July 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF mid-year needs and programme-monitoring report.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting; no independent impact evaluation.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, Northeast (Borno, Adamawa and Yobe) situation overview.
claims.paraphrase: The report describes combined conflict and early flooding across BAY; late-June rain submerged over 70% of Gumsuri in Damboa LGA, displacing hundreds.
claims.limitations: The report describes overlapping pressures but does not attribute flooding to conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF identifies conflict and flooding as concurrent BAY crisis drivers.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, Northwest (Katsina, Sokoto and Zamfara) situation overview.
claims.paraphrase: Rainy-season onset coincided with armed-group illegal taxes and restricted farmland access; localized floods destroyed homes and caused further displacement.
claims.limitations: The report does not separate the effects of rainfall and insecurity.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Rainy-season disruption and insecurity jointly complicated food access and displacement.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, BAY health-service and flooding section.
claims.paraphrase: In BAY, service access declined amid conflict, displacement and climate shocks; flood risk contaminated water and damaged health infrastructure, limiting care and raising disease risks.
claims.limitations: The report gives no facility-level comparison by hazard or conflict exposure.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF links access decline to combined conflict, displacement and climate shocks.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, Northwest disaster-management coordination paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF and disaster authorities held simulation workshops in Zamfara, Sokoto and Kebbi; a State-led coordination framework was being piloted in Zamfara.
claims.limitations: The pilot and workshops were ongoing; the report does not evaluate outcomes.

access_audit.locator: Opened all 14 PDF pages; claims use PDF pp. 2–4.
access_audit.notes: Original UNICEF report inspected. Cover gives 30 July 2025 and the reporting period 1 January–30 June 2025; claims remain historical.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

search_audit.outcome: The NiMet report was located but its 39.46 MB PDF could not be directly opened; extracted index text was excluded. UNICEF's directly opened report provides named local flood exposure.

search_audit.query: Nigeria 2025 climate flood conflict insecurity affected communities state report rainfall displaced people FCV official UN
search_audit.outcome: The opened UNICEF situation report documents contemporaneous early flooding and armed violence in BAY and Northwest regions without attributing one to the other.

search_audit.query: Nigeria climate shocks affect conflict displaced households host communities 2025 floods climate displacement report UNHCR official
search_audit.outcome: The directly opened UNICEF report describes reduced health access in BAY amid conflict, displacement and climate shocks, including flooding-related water and facility damage.

search_audit.query: Nigeria 2025 climate adaptation resilience capacity early warning local government flood plans NEMA NIHSA official
search_audit.outcome: The report records state disaster simulation workshops and a Zamfara-led coordination pilot; the NIHSA PDF returned 404 and the UN annual results PDF was too large to open.

gaps: No inspected source establishes climate as a cause of armed violence or farmer-herder conflict; UNICEF describes concurrent or interacting pressures.

The NiMet 2025 State of the Climate PDF was too large for direct web reading, the NIHSA 2025 flood-outlook link returned 404, and the UN 2024 results PDF was also too large; their search-index text was excluded.
The UNICEF report is a historical mid-year 2025 operational snapshot; response outputs and coordination pilots are not independent effectiveness evaluations.
